newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Iran to raise crude exports to China - NIOC.
newsitem.headline: Iran to raise crude exports to China - NIOC.

text.p: Iran's state-owned National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) is to raise crude exports to China to 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1998 and to 200,000 bpd in 2000, Ghanimi Fard, vice petroleum minister for trade, said on Tuesday.
Iran is currently exporting 70,000 bpd to China.
A deal to raise annual exports followed a visit in May to China by Iran's oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh.
Raising crude exports was part of the agenda for the visit to China.
Fard said the crude deal was for exports to rise to 100,000 bpd by 1998 and then to 200,000 bpd by 2000.
Iran is the second biggest producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) with a supply quota of 3.6 million bpd.
China has been laying the major planks of a long-term strategy to secure supplies into the next century.

China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) signed a $1.2 billion deal with Iraq to explore the one billion-barrel Ahdab field and a $3.5 billion deal with Kazakhstan for a 60-percent stake in Aktyubinskmunaigaz oil company.
The Kazakh deal includes building a 3,000-km (1,875 mile) pipeline to China.
At the same time, China has also said it plans to develop an oil reserve and might establish an oil tanker fleet to transport its crude.
Imports of crude are surging and could reach 34 million tonnes in 1997 versus 22 million in 1996, official Chinese media has reported this year.
